title: Dreamgirls
tagline: Three girls from Detroit, one spotlight, and the chicken comes out first.
about: In 1960s Detroit, three young singers are signed by an ambitious car salesman turned manager, and the climb to the top starts to pull them apart.
cue: Serve the snacks when the MC calls the Dreamettes the Creamettes.
faces: “$500 says the Dreamettes do not win.”
Three girls from Detroit, one spotlight, and the chicken comes out first.

Two drink minimum at the stage tables. Cover charge after nine. No discussing the Dreamettes being called the Creamettes at the tables. Card No. 1962. Showtime: Serve the snacks when the MC calls the Dreamettes the Creamettes.

Simmer, stirring, until thick and saucy, and season.Heat the dogs in a pan of barely simmering water.Warm the rolls, put a dog in each, spoon over the chilli and finish with a stripe of mustard and the rest of the onion.Effie's fried green tomatoes with hot sauce mayoThick slices of green tomato in a crunchy spiced polenta crust, fried golden, with hot sauce mayonnaiseHow to make it4 green tomatoes, in 1cm slices1 tsp salt125g mayonnaise1 tbsp hot sauce1 tsp lemon juice100g plain flour2 eggs125ml buttermilk120g fine polenta1 tsp sweet paprika1/2 tsp cayenne pepper250ml vegetable oil, for fryingSalt the tomato slices and leave on a rack for 10 minutes, then pat dry.Mix the mayonnaise, hot sauce and lemon juice.Set out the flour, then the eggs whisked with the buttermilk, then the polenta mixed with the paprika and cayenne. Coat each slice in all three.Shallow fry in the oil over medium high heat, in batches, for about 3 minutes a side until golden.Drain on paper towel, sprinkle with salt and serve hot with the hot sauce mayo.SupperRainbow Records Sunday fried chicken with baked mac and cheeseButtermilk-soaked chicken in a crisp spiced coating, fried deep golden, with baked cheddar macaroni and a crunchy crumb topHow to make it1.5kg chicken thighs and drumsticks, bone in500ml buttermilk2 tbsp hot sauce2 tsp salt250g plain flour, for the coating2 tsp sweet paprika1 tsp garlic powder1 tsp cayenne pepper1 tsp black pepper1.5 L vegetable oil, for frying300g macaroni40g butter3 tbsp plain flour, for the sauce600ml milk250g vintage cheddar, grated1 tsp mustard powder50g dry breadcrumbsWhisk the buttermilk, hot sauce and half the salt and turn the chicken through it.Marinate in the fridge.Boil the macaroni in salted water until just tender and drain.Melt the butter, stir in the sauce flour, then whisk in the milk until thick. Stir in most of the cheddar and the mustard powder and fold through the macaroni.Heat the oven to 180°C. Tip into a baking dish, top with the rest of the cheddar and the breadcrumbs and bake until golden and bubbling.Meanwhile heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 165°C. Mix the coating flour with the paprika, garlic powder, cayenne, pepper and the rest of the salt.Lift the chicken from the buttermilk, press firmly into the flour and fry in batches, turning, for 12 to 14 minutes until deep golden and cooked through.Drain on a rack for 5 minutes and serve with the mac and cheese.Curtis Taylor's payola pork chopsPan-fried and simmered in onion gravy, garlicky collard greens on the side, One Night OnlyHow to make it4 pork loin chops60g plain flour1 tsp smoked paprika3 tbsp vegetable oil2 brown onions500ml chicken stock1 bunch thyme1 bunch silverbeet or collard greens3 garlic cloves1 tbsp apple cider vinegarSeason the chops, dust in half the flour mixed with the paprika and brown in the oil for 3 minutes a side. Lift out.Fry the sliced onions in the same pan for 8 minutes until soft, stir in the rest of the flour, then whisk in the stock.Put the chops back with the thyme, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until tender in a thick gravy.Fry the sliced garlic in a little oil, add the shredded greens and a splash of water and cook for 6 minutes, then add the vinegar.Serve the chops smothered in gravy with the greens.After the ShowLorrell and Jimmy's sweet potato pieSilky spiced sweet potato custard in a crisp shortcrust case, with soft whipped creamHow to make it600g orange sweet potato, peeled and chunked1 sheet frozen shortcrust pastry60g butter, melted150g brown sugar2 eggs160ml evaporated milk1 tsp vanilla extract1 tsp ground cinnamon1/2 tsp ground nutmegpinch of salt300ml thickened creamBoil the sweet potato until very soft, drain well.Mash until completely smooth and cool slightly.Heat the oven to 180°C. Line a 23cm pie dish with the pastry, prick, line with baking paper and rice and blind bake, then remove the paper and rice.Whisk the sweet potato with the butter, sugar, eggs, evaporated milk, vanilla, spices and salt.Pour into the pastry case and bake until set at the edges with a slight wobble in the middle.Cool to room temperature.Whip the cream to soft peaks and serve with slices of the pie.From the BarNew Year's Eve 1966 champagne cocktailA sugar cube soaked in aromatic bitters under chilled sparkling wine with a twist of orangeHow to make it4 sugar cubes8 dashes of aromatic bitters600ml chilled sparkling wine1 orange, peel cut into 4 stripsDrop a sugar cube into each flute and soak it with 2 dashes of bitters.Top slowly with the sparkling wine.Twist a strip of orange peel over each glass and drop it in.
